title: Switch One Lamp, Count the Lamps That Are On

concept.title: A 0/1 array in a Fenwick tree: switching a lamp is adding +1 or -1, depending on its current state
body: A row of `n` lamps, each on (1) or off (0). One operation **switches** a single lamp (an on lamp goes off and an off lamp goes on). Another asks for the **number of lamps that are on** between the positions `x` and `y`. For the lamps `1 0 1 1` the count in the positions 2 to 4 is 2; after switching the lamp 2 it is 3.

The number of lamps that are on is the **sum** of the 0/1 values, so a Fenwick tree over the lamps answers the questions with two prefix sums. A switch changes the value of one cell by `+1` if the lamp was off and `-1` if it was on, that is `1 - 2 * state`. Keep an array with the current state of every lamp, update it, and add the change to the tree.
The idea generalises to every "toggle" structure over an additive quantity (parity changes, on/off flags). The program makes O(log n) steps per operation, so O((n + q) log n) in total.

statement: A row of `n` lamps (0 = off, 1 = on) is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x x` switches the lamp `x`; type 2 `x y` asks how many lamps from `x` to `y` are on. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of lamps and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers, each 0 or 1: the lamps (1 = on).
Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, switch the lamp `x` (`y` equals `x`). If `t = 2`, print how many lamps from `x` to `y` are on.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: Lamps are numbered from 1; for a count 1 <= x <= y <= n.

examples.note: Two lamps are on in 2..4; after the switch of the lamp 2 there are three: 2 3.

hints: The count of lamps that are on is a sum of 0/1 values.
A switch adds +1 for an off lamp and -1 for an on lamp.
Keep the state of each lamp in an array.

explanation: The lamps are a 0/1 array in a Fenwick tree; a switch adds +1 or -1 according to the current state, and a count is the difference of two prefix sums.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).
